clauses.current_legal_basis: Original-plus-bounded-search route. The held Federal Register text of EO 12423 (48 FR 24025) is read in full; it has no expiry date or terminating condition. EO 12163 section 1-301(b), which section 1 amends, has no held later rewrite: EO 12458 section 2, EO 12560 sections 7 and 8, EO 12639 section 6, EO 12680 section 4, EO 12738 section 5, EO 13091 section 3 and EO 13118 section 3 change other subsections of 1-301. The bounded searches current-law:usc (2 hits: the 22 U.S.C. 2381 note printing EO 12163's status line, which lists EO 12423 among its amendments, and the 22 U.S.C. 2751 note whose ended status line for EO 11958 lists EO 12423; edition current through 2026-10-09), current-law:ecfr (0 hits; point-in-time as of 2026-10-14) and later-events:ofr_catalog (0 hits) located no instrument that amends, revokes or supersedes EO 12423 or EO 12163 section 1-301(b).
clauses.reason: Section 1 amends section 1-301(b) of EO 12163 by adding section 636(i) to the functions listed there. Under the strike-and-insert ruling the amendment continues, as amended, while the parent stands. EO 12163 remains in force; no held later instrument rewrites 1-301(b) (later amendments touch other subsections); and EO 13637 revokes EO 11958, not EO 12163. Operative on 2026-10-14.

Section 2 amended section 1(d) of EO 11958 to delegate the functions under sections 22(a), 29 and 30 of the Act to the Secretary of Defense. EO 12560 section 11 (signed May 24, 1986; 51 FR 19159) restated 1(d) with the same delegation plus section 30A; under the strike-and-insert ruling that is an amendment recorded as a later event, and a human reviewer should note the substance changed. The clause ended when section 4 of EO 13637 of March 8, 2013 (78 FR 16129) revoked EO 11958 of January 18, 1977 as amended. EO 13637 has no deferred-effect wording, so the revocation took effect on signing, 2013-03-08; the alternative reading is publication on March 13, 2013. EO 13637 section 1(d) re-delegates the same functions, so the delegation continues under that order, not under EO 12423.

research_rationale:
EO 12423 of May 26, 1983, Foreign Assistance and Arms Control (48 FR 24025, FR Doc. 83-14689), was read in full from the held Federal Register text. It has two operative sections, both amendments of other orders: section 1 adds section 636(i) to the functions listed in section 1-301(b) of EO 12163; section 2 restates section 1(d) of EO 11958 as a delegation to the Secretary of Defense of the functions under sections 22(a), 29 and 30 of the Act. Under the owner's strike-and-insert ruling (2026-10-21) an amendment clause continues, as amended, until the parent order ends. EO 12163 remains in force and no held later instrument rewrites subsection 1-301(b), so section 1 is operative on 2026-10-14. EO 11958 was revoked as amended by section 4 of EO 13637 of March 8, 2013, with its substance re-delegated in section 1(d) of EO 13637, so section 2 ended on 2013-03-08. EO 12560 section 11 (May 24, 1986) earlier restated section 1(d) to add the functions under section 30A; that amends the clause without ending it, and a human reviewer should note that the substance changed. The whole order is YES because section 1 is operative. The dossier chain lists many other amenders of EO 12163 and EO 11958; they are not later events of EO 12423 unless they change 1-301(b) or 1(d), and EO 13637 does not name EO 12163.

savings.reason: Section 2's delegation to the Secretary of Defense of the functions under sections 22(a), 29, 30 and 30A of the Arms Export Control Act was carried forward when EO 11958 was revoked: section 1(d) of EO 13637 delegates those functions to the Secretary of Defense, and section 4 of EO 13637 continues actions taken under EO 11958 to the extent consistent with it. The delegation survives under EO 13637, not under EO 12423 section 2.
